review_candidates.title: Chief Financial Officer
review_candidates.description: The Autism Society of North Carolina (ASNC) is seeking an experienced financial leader to serve as its Chief Financial Officer (CFO), guiding the organization’s financial strategy and operations at a pivotal time of growth. Reporting directly to and partnering closely with the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), the CFO will serve as a trusted thought partner and integral member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT), helping shape and deliver on ASNC’s mission and strategic priorities. This role champions the integration of sound business analytics, data-driven decision-making, and process automation — modernizing legacy financial systems to improve accuracy, efficiency, and visibility across the organization. This is an outstanding opportunity to drive positive change in a critically important, mission-driven organization, touching hundreds of thousands of lives each year. ASNC operates a complex, diversified financial model with approximately $34 million in annual revenue, generated primarily through Medicaid and commercial insurance reimbursement, complemented by approximately $3 million in annual philanthropic support. The CFO will play a critical role in optimizing this model, strengthening revenue cycle performance, evaluating service-line economics, and ensuring the long-term financial sustainability of the organization. The CFO directly supervises the Accounting Manager, Revenue Cycle Manager, Finance Manager, and Director of Property and Facilities, and is accountable for the performance, development, and coordination of their respective teams. The broader finance/accounting team comprises a total of 10 staff. The Property and Facility Management team has six additional staff. Candidate Profile: Minimum of 10 years of progressive financial leadership experience, including at least 5 years in a senior finance role (CFO, VP of Finance, or equivalent) within an organization of comparable size and complexity ($30M–$50M+ annual revenue); an active CPA license is strongly preferred. Experience with modern, cloud-based ERP and HRIS platforms (e.g., NetSuite, Paycom) and business intelligence tools (e.g., Power BI) is strongly preferred, along with a demonstrated ability to leverage technology to modernize legacy financial processes. Significant experience in healthcare, human services, behavioral health, IDD, or another reimbursement-driven environment involving Medicaid, managed care, commercial insurance, or other third-party payers is strongly preferred. While it is understood that no candidate will offer every desired skill, quality, and characteristic, the following competencies offer a detailed, aspirational view of the ideal candidate profile: Key Responsibilities Financial Expertise and Strategic Leadership • Serve as a strategic financial advisor to the executive team and Board of Directors, providing forecasting, analysis, and insight to guide long-term organizational strategy. • Play a key role in developing and executing strategic priorities that advance the organization’s mission and financial objectives. • Lead financial planning and analysis, including building and maintaining financial projections, periodic forecasts, and the annual budget. • Provide comprehensive financial updates to senior management and the Finance Committee to ensure transparency, accountability, and informed decisionmaking. • Manage banking relationships, including working with lenders on financing agreements, and with cash management personnel to maximize resources. • Lead the zero-based annual budget process, partnering with program managers to build budgets, training staff on financial oversight, and supporting funder reporting. • Conduct ongoing financial analysis of current services to identify weaknesses and opportunities. • Partner with the Chief Development Officer and Development team on grant proposals and reporting. • Partner with the Chief Program and Policy Officer and Chief Operating Officer on rate negotiations, start-up budgets, and other programmatic budget needs. • Oversee administration and optimization of dashboards and business intelligence tools, providing leadership and the Board of Directors with real-time visibility into financial performance, KPIs, and operational trends. • Execute additional finance and accounting duties as directed by the CEO. • Partner with the Compliance Officer on fraud, waste, and abuse prevention, including False Claims Act risk areas. Revenue Cycle Management • Oversee revenue cycle functions, including Medicaid and private-pay billing, collections, and reimbursement processes, ensuring timely and accurate revenue recognition. • Direct claims denial management, appeals processes, and resolution of billing discrepancies. • Monitor key revenue cycle metrics, including days in accounts receivable, collection rates, and payer mix. • Prepare and submit Medicaid Waiver Cost Reports to DHHS Division of Health Benefits and the Office of the Controller. • Maintain financial practices consistent with HIPA Financial Systems, Technology, Compliance, and Reporting • Manage the relationship with the audit firm(s) for the audit of the annual financial statements and 401(k) plan. • Leverage ASNC’s core financial technology stack — NetSuite (ERP), Paycom (payroll/HR), and Power BI (business intelligence and reporting) — to drive automation, data integrity, and real- time financial visibility. • Serve as 401(k) plan administrator/trustee and member of the 401(k) Investment Committee, including filing Form 5500 for the 401(k) and Health and Welfare plans. • Compile cost and profit analysis, including requests for enhanced rates to Health Plans (commercial and Medicaid). • Manage cash accounts and endowment funds, including oversight and evaluation of investment managers and accounts. • Oversee grant and contract execution, reporting, business insurance, and employee benefits administration. • Ensure the integrity of financial statements and internal controls, and maintain compliance with GAAP, FASB nonprofit accounting standards, 2 CFR 200 (Uniform Guidance), and applicable federal, state, and grantor requirements. • Establish and enforce accounting and financial policies and procedures, ensuring alignment with state licensing and accreditation requirements. • Complete NC Personal Property tax returns and manage the tax exemption process for properties and vehicles.
